title: DeepMind's new lead says AI agents now run parts of Gemini model training under human supervision
subtitle: Koray Kavukcuoglu told The Information's AI Agenda Live Summit that agents are already conducting experiments, analyzing results and proposing hypotheses — work he says wasn't being done this way six months ago.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Koray Kavukcuoglu, who stepped up as SVP of Google DeepMind after Demis Hassabis moved to Alphabet chief scientist, told The Information's AI Agenda Live Summit that agents are now running parts of model training — designing and running experiments, analyzing results, and proposing new hypotheses — with humans supervising. He said the approach wasn't in use six months earlier. Gemini 4 is in an early phase of post-training, he said, and he wants to ship it 'much earlier' than the end of the year.

The admission is less about one benchmark and more about who is writing the training recipe. DeepMind is saying, on the record, that the loop which once belonged entirely to human researchers — pick a hypothesis, run an ablation, read the result, pick the next hypothesis — is being partly handed to agents. The humans still supervise, but they are no longer in every seat. Separate reporting from Capital Brief says Kavukcuoglu has personally formed a strike team of engineers and researchers aimed at improving DeepMind's coding models.

This is the point the field has been circling since Anthropic's October 'dreaming' feature and OpenAI's Erdős-problem claim: the loop that trains the next model is becoming a target for the current model. When you compress that loop, the rate at which capability compounds changes — not linearly, but in jumps. Whether this is already happening at scale inside Google is a question Kavukcuoglu answered yes to, which no frontier lab leader had said that plainly before.

A note for learners: 'agents doing research' means something specific here — running experiments inside an ML training pipeline, not writing a paper. If you are early in your career, the skill that becomes scarcer is not running the experiment; it is defining the experiment, choosing what to measure, and judging the result. Learn to supervise an agent that's faster than you at the mechanical part.
